Subject: Nebula — reservation option matrix and phased activation plan

Julia —

Thanks again for the meeting earlier. Per our conversation, I put together three reservation option sketches you can evaluate with procurement and engineering. Each option includes: cluster footprint (GPU count), minimum guaranteed GPUs, expected ramp cadence, and an illustration of burst windows. The attached workbook has line-item SKUs and a week-by-week ramp graphic. High-level options below: 

1) Stability Floor (Conservative)
- Cluster: 8x A800-equivalent GPUs (single pool)
- Min guaranteed: 6 GPUs always available
- Ramp: month 1 = 6, month 2 = 6-8 (activate burst lanes), month 3+ = 8 steady
- Good for predictable batch inference and steady throughput; lowest on-demand overage risk

2) Balanced Throughput (Balanced)
- Cluster: 16x A800-equivalent GPUs (2 pools for canary + prod)
- Min guaranteed: 10 GPUs (elastic burst to 16 during peak windows)
- Ramp: week-by-week activation: 2 GPUs/week for first 4 weeks, then 1 GPU/week until month 3 cap
- Recommended if you need runway for model experimentation while controlling baseline spend

3) Growth + Bursting (Aggressive)
- Cluster: 32x A800-equivalent GPUs (multi-pool, cross-region-ready)
- Min guaranteed: 12 GPUs (reserved) with committed burst lanes to 32 under SLA
- Ramp: phase 1 (first 30 days) reserve 12; phase 2 (days 31-90) progressive activation to 32 per usage triggers; optional scheduled bursts for experiments
- Best for customers expecting rapid product-driven growth and large inference spikes

Key trade-offs and ops notes:
- Autoscaling cadence: we recommend 5–10 minute autoscale windows for the Balanced option; Conservative can use 15+ minute windows
- Prefix/KV cache sizing: Larger clusters allow more KV cache per model instance — call this out if you have long-context traffic
- Cross-region replication: additional cluster for DR (recommended once committed GPUs > 24)

Next steps I suggest: pick preferred option and a 90-day phased activation milestone table; we can convert the chosen option into a draft MOU with rates and breakpoints. I attached the SKU matrix and a ramp diagram for quick review.

Would love your preference and any procurement constraints (billing cadence, PO lead time, required invoice language).

Best,

Mina — notes below for the one-pager and numbers you can send back to Julia: 

1) Balanced run-rate (example) — assume A800-equivalent pricing tier: 
- Month 1: Reserved 10 GPUs (baseline) — monthly reserved fee $56,000; expected usage mix covers ~70% of tokens on reserve; incremental token cost $0.0016 per 1k tokens; estimated overage spend $6,500 (conservative)
- Month 2: Reserve 12 GPUs (activated 2 additional); monthly reserved fee $67,200; expected overage $4,000
- Month 3: Reserve 14 GPUs (steady at activation cap 16 when needed); monthly reserved fee $78,400; expected overage $2,000

2) Scheduled burst windows — we can support SLA-backed scheduled bursts as an add-on. Terms: guaranteed reserved mini-alloc for up to 8 hours/day during a 30-day scheduled window. Pricing: +18% on the baseline reserved fee for any month containing guaranteed burst windows; requires signed amendment 7 days prior to the window and operational playbook.

3) VPC/private deployment footprint — for PHI lanes we recommend bumping the min guaranteed GPUs by ~20% over public-hosted numbers to ensure redundancy and failover (recommended min guaranteed becomes 12 instead of 10 for the Balanced example). The increase covers dedicated HA margins and additional DR replication nodes. This is standard for customers with strict compliance and HA needs.

4) Lead times / start date — Jan 1 target looks feasible if LOI received by 2026-11-19 and we get a 2-week runway to provision dedicated pools and run a smoke validation. Procurement items: PO terms, invoice cadence (monthly), and SOC2 attestation copy on file.

I've attached a short sample cost table and a diagram for the ramp activation. Tweak language for procurement and send it back to Julia.

Julia —

Thanks for the great questions. Attached is a one-page run-rate & SLA note that pulls together the Balanced example Ben outlined and a short section on scheduled bursts and VPC sizing. Executive summary:

- Recommendation: start on Balanced Throughput with an initial 10-GPU reserved baseline and a 90-day ramp to 14–16 GPUs. If you require PHI lanes in a VPC, we recommend setting the baseline to 12 reserved GPUs to cover HA.
- Scheduled bursts: available as an SLA add-on (guaranteed mini-reservation for scheduled windows). Pricing premium: +18% on reserved fee months containing guaranteed bursts. Amendment required 7 days prior to scheduled window.
- Jan 1 start: feasible with LOI by 2026-11-19 and completed PO by 2026-12-15. Provisioning timeline includes cluster build, KMS integration for VPC, and smoke validation.

Next steps: please confirm (a) whether you want VPC PHI lanes (we'll set baseline=12 if yes), (b) whether you want the scheduled-burst SLA on launch, and (c) a preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly). Once you confirm, I'll circulate an MOU draft and a DocuSign link for the LOI.
